_about: Prices and limits. Market prices drift 80-130% of 'market_base' each morning.
_about_balance: Tuned on 2026-11-15 for the 20-minute day (Alex: money should always feel meaningful and hard to get). Sweaters are the economy (Alex, 2026-11-15): every coin she earns comes from a sweater, sold to anyone in town face to face ('haggle'), to Rosa at the day's price, posted from the mailbox at the plain 'sell_prices' price, by mail order or for a local's request. Crops, wool and wild fibre can't be sold: crops are to eat, wool and fibre to knit. Jobs pay petty cash and drop something useful ('jobs' 'loot'). With two sheep and Gran's needles a day earns about 150c before rent, food and wool, so the first better needles take about three days. Every number is a draft.
_about_haggle: Selling a sweater to anyone in town (scripts/sweater_sale.gd; Alex, 2026-11-15). Asked once a day, a villager is looking for one with chance 'yes_base' plus 'yes_per_heart' for each heart and 'yes_per_trust' for each point of trust, or only 'rebuy_yes' if they bought one in the last 'rebuy_days' days. If they are, she sets a price: the meter shows how likely they are to say yes. Each villager has a hidden top price for the day, 'res_min'..'res_max' times the sweater's fair price (Rosa's price for its rarity) plus 'res_per_heart' for each heart; at it the chance is even, and 'spread' (a share of the fair price) sets how fast it falls off. An offer they turn down within 'counter_within' of their top price gets a counter-offer; after 'tries' refusals they walk away for the day. 'step' is the price buttons' step.

story._about: Act 1 (scripts/homestead.gd): Nora arrives with nothing; Gran's note leaves her 'gran_coins' (0 since 2026-11-16: she leaves her yarn and needles, and Wren buying the first sweater is the first money). Rent for Gran's house ('rent' coins every 'rent_days' days) goes in Gran's tin. Steve at Builder's Delight sells 'wood_pack' wood for 'wood_pack_price'. A fence panel takes 'fence_wood' wood; a gate is crafted (data/recipes.json). Max, her ex, visits the farm once she has played 'max_visit_hours' hours (main.gd _update_max_visit, data/scenes/max.scene). Lars, next door, rents her the barn for her animals: 'barn_rent' coins every 'barn_rent_days' days (a month), from the day her first sheep are penned; she pays him in person (homestead.gd).

land.name: Eastfield Acres
land.pitch: Twenty flat acres of sweet grass. Room for a hundred sheep and a barn you could hold a wedding in.

land.name: Greyspine Hollow
land.pitch: A stone cottage, a spring and a view of the whole range. The fog comes in like a postcard.

land.name: Saltmeadow Point
land.pitch: Sea on three sides. Sunsets you can sell tickets to. The crown jewel, and I don't say that about everything. I say it about most things.

_about_land: Gary's listings at Willow Homes (main.land_plots): shown on his menu and pitched on his visits to the farm (data/scenes/town.scene). Out of reach early on by design, and not for sale yet: buying land is still to come. Names, prices and pitches are drafts for Alex.
_about_building: Walls she builds in build mode (scripts/house_builder.gd; Alex, 2026-11-15): 'wall' and 'door' (a doorway) are coins a 2 m length, paid as each goes up. A room is about three days of sweater sales: a 4 x 4 m room against the house takes six walls (480c), the old 8 x 4 'Expand House' about 640c. Taking one down gives 'refund' of its price back. 'plots' are building plots Gary sells at Willow Homes ([x, z, width, depth], on the even grid), a little cheaper for each of his hearts; the first wall of a new house on one also pays 'new_house_fee' for the foundations. 'plot_sold' are Gary's lines. 'recolor' is what a new colour for a piece of furniture costs (data/furniture.json 'palettes'). Every number and line is a draft for Alex.

plot_sold: Sold! Lane's yours, or the brook's, I lose track. Mine says SOLD now either way. I'll have the lads clear it by morning. By this afternoon. By the time you get there.
Congratulations, you're a landowner. Foundations are on you, walls are on you, the view's on the house. Not literally. You'll need a house.

jobs._about_loot: Alex, 2026-11-15: jobs aren't for money. They pay a little petty cash and build the boss's familiarity and trust (requests come with hearts), and every full shift drops one thing from 'loot', picked by 'weight': 'item' goes in her bag ('n' is [least, most]); 'piece' is a piece of furniture she can place from the catalogue for nothing.
jobs._about: Jobs beside knitting (scripts/jobs.gd): petty cash, the boss's friendship and a random drop for a shift at someone's workplace. She holds one job at a time and works at most one shift a day. 'boss' offers it: the scene 'job_<id>' (data/scenes/jobs.scene) plays the first time she talks to them once the offer is due (after Act 1, and once their trust reaches 'trust' if given); if she says no, the boss's menu keeps a 'Take the job' row. She clocks in by talking to the boss between 'start' [from, to] o'clock. A shift walks her through 'tasks' 'rounds' times ('at' is where she stands and 'face' what she turns to, [x, z] in the 'building's own space, its front toward +z; 'secs' is how long each takes), or with 'round': true to every door in town. The clock moves on 'hours' over the shift, 'drain' comes off her needs spread over it, 'pay' coins at the end (part of it if she stops early), and a full shift adds 'perk' to her needs. 'lines' are what the boss says at the start and the end. Names, pay and lines are drafts for Alex.

bakery.name: Heart Bakery
bakery.perk_text: Giorgio sends you home with a warm loaf.

start: Apron's on the hook. Oven first, then the flour, then we'll see who comes in.
Six on the dot. Good. The dough noticed.
Wash your hands, cara. Then wash them again. Then bread.
done: Good work. Here, take this loaf. Don't argue, it's already wrapped.
You were quiet today. Quiet's fine. The bread came out right.
That's the morning. Go home, eat, sleep. In that order.

cafe.name: Cappuccino Cafe
cafe.perk_text: Sabrina slides you a coffee. 'It was going to waste. Probably.'

start: You're on the terrace. Don't drop anything. Or do, and I'll watch.
Tables one and two. That's all of them. Go.
Okay. Shift. Try to look like you like people.
done: You didn't break anything. Weird. Good weird.
Here's your money. Don't spend it on yarn. You will, though.
Same time tomorrow, if you want. I don't care. Come, though.

post.name: the post round
post.perk_text: Barbara tucks a peppermint into your pocket.

start: Here's your half of the bag, sweetheart. Every door, and a smile for whoever opens it.
Letters are lighter if you whistle. Try it.
Good shoes? Good. Off you go.
done: All delivered? That's a town that heard from someone today, thanks to you.
You walk like you're going somewhere now. That's new.
The round brings you back, sweetheart. It always does.

_about_store: Builder's Delight (Steve): her tools, seeds and wood over the counter (Alex, 2026-11-14: a new game starts with only Gran's shears). 'tools' is tool id -> price; 'seeds' is crop id -> [seeds in a packet, price]; 'seed_tin' is what Gran's seed tin on the kitchen counter holds. 'wool_packs_a_day' is how many packs of wool Rosa will sell her in one day, so her own animals matter.
_about_gear: What her money buys to knit better and go further (scripts/empire.gd; Alex, 2026-11-15). 'lantern': Steve's price for the lantern that lights her way at night. 'needles': better pairs, in order, sold by Rosa one step at a time; 'floor' is the least a sweater knitted with them can be (1 Common .. 5 Legendary). 'first_needles' is what she starts with. Names, prices and lines are drafts.

needles.name: Steel needles
needles.line: Steel, love. They don't bend and they don't snag. You'll feel the difference by the second row.

needles.name: Rosewood needles
needles.line: Rosewood. Warm in the hand. My own mother knitted with a pair just like these.

needles.name: Silver needles
needles.line: Silver. I've had these in the case eleven years waiting for someone good enough. Go on, they're yours.

_about_forage: Her axe and shears out in the world (scripts/forage.gd): a felled tree gives 'tree_wood' and grows back after 'tree_regrow_days'; a trimmed plant gives 'leaves' by kind (the start of its model name) and grows back after 'plant_regrow_days'. 'mulch_leaves' leaves mulch a growing bed, bringing it on by 'mulch_growth' of its whole growing time. Trees in Maple Grove itself aren't hers to fell.

bonfire._about: Bonfires (scripts/bonfire.gd, Alex 2026-11-17): she lights one on open ground from dusk (from_hour) to dawn for half a tree's wood (forage tree_wood 8 / 2). It burns until the next dawn. While one burns, midnight doesn't put her to sleep: the night goes on until morning. Within warm_radius metres her warmth heads for at least `warmth`; light_range is how far its light reaches; warm_up is what 'Warm up by the fire' gives. 'Sleep by the fire' sleeps her there till 6:00 like bed but gives back only sleep_rest energy (half a night's rest), so she needn't walk home to bed. Numbers are drafts.

fog._about: The fog over unexplored land (scripts/fog_of_war.gd, Alex 2026-11-17): everything outside a circle round the farm and Maple Grove (centre [x, z], radius, then fade metres to full fog) is under a light fog until she, or the dog she plays, has been within reveal metres of it. cell is the explored grid's cell in metres; top is the fog layer's height; density and max_alpha set how thick it looks (max_alpha < 1: you always see through it).
